preconditions.description: The input consists of exactly two lines.
The number of denominations n is an integer between 2 and 100 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(coins) == n and coins[0] == 1 and all(coins[i] < coins[i+1] for i in range(n-1)) and coins[-1] <= 10**6
preconditions.description: The denominations are n distinct positive integers sorted in strictly increasing order, starting with 1, and the largest is at most 10^6.

postconditions.description: The output is 'canonical' if the greedy algorithm yields the optimal number of coins for every positive integer amount, and 'non-canonical' otherwise.

postconditions.expression: is_canonical == all(greedy_count(x, coins) == optimal_count(x, coins) for x in range(1, coins[-1] + coins[-2]))
postconditions.description: The system is canonical if and only if for all amounts x less than the sum of the two largest denominations, the number of coins used by the greedy algorithm equals the minimum number of coins required.
